title: Roll a cabinet shelf wider than its face-frame opening through it, level it inside, and lower it onto its four pins
instruction: Put the shelf in the cabinet on its four pins.
context: The shelf is wider than the way in. A kitchen wall cabinet's face frame narrows its opening to 305 mm, while the shelf is 340 mm wide to span the 343 mm inside. So it goes in rolled about 35 degrees, is pushed in past the frame, and is rolled level about its own centre, with 1.5 mm to spare at each side. Then it comes down onto four 5 mm pins, all four together, square and back against the back panel; pushed in short, or levelled with one end caught under its pins, it falls past them. Shelving tasks on open shelves slide a board straight on; here the opening is narrower than the board. People put shelves back this way whenever a kitchen cabinet is moved or cleaned out.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of the table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A 15 in (381 mm) wide, 12 in (305 mm) deep, 18 in (457 mm) tall face-frame wall cabinet stands on the table, fixed to it, its opening towards the robot and its middle at (61, 0): 19 mm white melamine sides, top and bottom, a 6 mm back, and a 19 mm wood face frame whose 38 mm stiles and 38 mm rails narrow the opening to 305 mm wide and 381 mm tall; inside it is 343 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Four 5 mm brass shelf pins stand 6 mm out of the sides, 37 mm from the inside's front and back, their axes 20 cm above the table. The shelf, 16 mm white melamine particleboard, 340 x 265 mm, 0.98 kg, lies on two foam blocks, 200 x 60 mm and 90 mm tall, fixed to the table at y +15.5 and -15.5 and centred at x 34.8, in front of the cabinet, where it was set down while the cabinet was moved, its long side along y and its front edge at x 18.5.
scoring: Spirit level, feeler gauge and photo. At the end, held 1 s: the shelf's underside within 1 mm of all four pin tops; roll and pitch within 1 degree; square to the sides within 1 degree; its back edge within 10 mm of the back panel (pushed home, as a fitter leaves it: its front edge then stands 5 to 15 mm behind the face frame, not against it; on all four pins the shelf can lie anywhere in a 15 mm range, and since four-pin contact within 1 mm already makes it level and square, this gap is what separates 1.0 from 0.5); both grippers more than 3 cm from it. 1.0: all of these, held 1 s. 0.5: all of these but not yet held 1 s when the run ends, or on all four pins but not level, square or fully back. 0.25: inside the cabinet, on three pins or above the pin row. 0: outside the cabinet, on its floor, or a gripper within 3 cm of it; 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: The shelf on its two foam blocks at its marks; the pins pushed fully into their holes. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. Cabinet, frame and pins are fixed boxes and 12-sided pin hulls; the shelf is one free box, friction 0.5 (not measured). The cabinet is a stock 15 in wall cabinet's width and depth, 18 in tall to stay in the arms' reach. Pins do not come out of their holes.
